deities: Goddess Ghanteswari (form of Shakti/Durga, worshipped as the Goddess of Bells)

history.summary: Maa Ghanteswari Temple is the famous 'temple of bells' on the bank of the Mahanadi at Chipilima (also spelled Chiplima/Chipilama, Bagbira), in Sambalpur district, western Odisha - it is the best-known shrine of the village, often called the 'Heart of Chipilima'. Devotees offer bells (ghanti) to the goddess after their wishes are fulfilled, so thousands of bells hang across the complex. Local tradition holds that before the Hirakud Dam was built, the bells rang in the wind and warned sailors of dangerous currents and whirlpools at the confluence of the Mahanadi, Malti and Baby rivers, earning it the title 'lighthouse without light'. The exact date of construction is unknown (verify). CSV corrections: town 'Sambalpur' corrected to Chipilima - the temple is not in Sambalpur city but about 25-33 km away (sources vary: odishantemples says ~25 km, several sources say ~33 km south-west; verify exact figure), near the Chipilima Hydro Power Plant (CHEP); a bridge at Mundoghat (Chaurpur Bridge, functional since December 2018) improved access from Sambalpur. District (Sambalpur) and state (Odisha) are correct. Coordinates are the Chipilima locality (verify exact temple point).

name: Maa Ghanteswari Temple
town_description: Chipilima (also spelled Chiplima/Chipilama) is a village and picnic spot in Sambalpur district, western Odisha, on the bank of the Mahanadi near the Chipilima Hydro Electric Project, about 25-33 km south-west of Sambalpur city.

travel.airport: Veer Surendra Sai Airport, Jharsuguda, approximately 50-70 km north (verify); Biju Patnaik International Airport, Bhubaneswar, is a farther option.
travel.railway: Sambalpur Junction, approximately 25-33 km north-east (verify exact distance).
travel.road: On the Chipilima road from Sambalpur via NH 6 / the Chaurpur Bridge at Mundoghat (functional since December 2018), near the Chipilima Hydro Power Plant; a narrow iron bridge across a power channel leads to the temple.

visitor_information.best_time: October to March, when the weather is cooler (per regional travel guides).
visitor_information.opening_hours: Daily approximately 4:00 AM to 8:00 PM (verify - from a travel video description; confirm locally).
